quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Be visible.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless following or meeting another car), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective materials to be seen. Change your lane position as needed to see well, be seen, and have enough space around you.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax on the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handgrips firmly. Ease off the throttle and ride straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake to the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid road hazards.
Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Increase your ability to be seen by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see and be seen by others, keep you out of blind spots, help you avoid hazards, protect your lane from other drivers, show your intentions, help you avoid wind from other vehicles, and give you an escape route.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is likely to be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs show rules and regulations, such as speed limits. They are white with black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only sometimes.
Only when riding in the city.
Every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time.
questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the most stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake of the tire that is flat.
Apply both brakes.
Not use either brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake to the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter to apply the brake when downshifting.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when you use either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes get pressure. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.
Behind the left footrest.
Behind the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest and is operated by your left foot. Lift your foot under the lever to shift up to a higher gear. Press the lever down to downshift.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, which is correct?

options.text: The pass may be completed in a no passing zone.
You may travel up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
The pass must be started and completed in a passing zone.
The pass must be completed on the shoulder if one is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pass must be started and completed in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: Always pass within the posted speed limit and only in areas where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: As the motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, what happens?

options.text: You can apply the front brake harder.
You should use less pressure on the front brake.
You can apply the rear brake harder.
You lose traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When you brake, your weight shifts forward, and the front wheel gets more grip. This means you can apply the front brake harder.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may pull out suddenly into your path.
Other drivers may move slowly while looking for parking.
The road surface may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may pull out suddenly into your path.
questions.explanation: A driver might pull out of a parking space without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between parked cars.

questions.question: How should you control your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright.
Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: Look ahead through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before turning. Lean your motorcycle in the correct direction.

questions.question: What should you consider when choosing your lane position?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which lane position makes your trip shorter.
Which position lets you pass more vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers. Also make sure you have enough space around you.

questions.question: What should you do when being passed?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the left side of the lane.
Ride in the right side of the lane.
Move between different parts of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to merge back too soon.

questions.question: Why is checking your motorcycle important?

options.text: Only a mechanic can do a useful check.
You should not check it before a ride.
Check it only after you ride.
It helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures that could be dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend wants to ride after drinking?

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to use less busy roads.
Push their motorcycle over.
Ask other friends to convince them not to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask other friends to convince them not to ride.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride if they have been drinking. Do everything you can to stop them. It helps to get a group of friends to talk to them about not riding.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Every time you change lanes.
Only when it is dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is dry.
When the pavement is wet.
When you can see through the vehicle ahead.
When the sun is shining.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your distance when your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Wet pavement, blocked visibility, or heavy traffic all require more space between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When a group passes a vehicle on a two-lane road, how should riders pass?

options.text: Pass in pairs.
Pass in a staggered formation with multiple riders passing at once.
Pass one rider at a time.
Avoid passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass one rider at a time.
questions.explanation: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. Each rider must complete their pass before the next rider begins.

questions.question: How should you make a quick stop on wet pavement?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on a slippery surface. Apply the front brake gradually to prevent it from locking.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action first, then the other. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve, but not both.
Do not swerve. Only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do one action at a time. Do not brake while swerving because this may cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: What can help if your drive chain slips?

options.text: Tighten the chain
Loosen the chain
Use more throttle
Apply the rear brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Tighten the chain
questions.explanation: Tightening the chain may fix chain slippage. If tightening does not work, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black letters or symbols are warning signs. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: How much stopping power does the front brake provide on a motorcycle?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
100 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If you must brake while turning, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you finish the turn to brake.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: When turning, your tires have less grip. Always straighten out your motorcycle before braking if possible. If you must brake while turning, apply the brakes slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: When should a rider check their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly
When stopped at an intersection
When changing lanes
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, when stopped at an intersection, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: How should you cross railroad tracks that run along the road?

options.text: Cross at a 90-degree angle.
Never cross the tracks.
Cross at about a 45-degree angle.
Cross very slowly, inch by inch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross at about a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks, trolley tracks, or pavement seams at an angle of at least 45 degrees. Make a quick, sharp turn. Crossing slowly or at a shallow angle can catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: How do you lean a motorcycle to turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip away from the direction you want to turn.
Apply the front brake.
Apply the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles lean to turn. To lean your motorcycle, press on the handgrip in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a tire go flat. A sudden change in how the motorcycle handles is a more common sign of tire failure.

questions.question: How do you stop in the shortest distance on a straight road?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straight road, use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance. Do not lock either brake.

questions.question: When you stop, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: On the right side of the lane.
On the left side of the lane.
As close as possible to the vehicle in front.
Without signaling so you do not distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. Signal your intentions and check for traffic. Pass when it is safe, then signal and return to your original lane.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hand ready on the clutch and brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.
Ride below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hand ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hand ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to dangers.

questions.question: What do most headache, cold, and hay fever medications do to your body?

options.text: Make you sleepy.
Make you more awake.
Make you hungry.
Make you unable to focus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you sleepy.
questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or nerves cause drowsiness and may affect your riding ability. Know how a medication affects you before you ride.

questions.question: How much maintenance does a motorcycle need compared to a car?

options.text: Less frequent maintenance than a car.
More frequent maintenance than a car.
Pre-ride checks only by a mechanic.
Service only at a dealer.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent maintenance than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle more often. Do a thorough check before every ride.

questions.question: When riding at night, which is NOT something you should do?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Increase your distance from other vehicles.
Decrease your distance from other vehicles.
Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Reduce speed and increase your following distance at night to avoid crashes. Use headlights ahead to see farther. Use your high beam headlight unless you are following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: What is true about low-speed crashes?

options.text: They can be fatal.
They are never serious.
They rarely cause injuries.
They happen often, so do not worry about them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be fatal.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds under 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be fatal.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
At the back of the group.
Wherever they feel most comfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front. This lets experienced riders watch them from the back of the group.

questions.question: How do you lean a motorcycle into a turn?

options.text: Always press the left handgrip.
Always press the right handgrip.
Press the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn, a motorcycle must lean. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean.

questions.question: Alcohol impairment starts:

options.text: Well before the legal limit.
At the legal limit.
Just above the legal limit.
Well above the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Well before the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Your riding skills get worse well before you reach the legal limit.

questions.question: If your motorcycle wobbles, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Brake right away.
Hold the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up or brake during a wobble—both make it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by gradually closing the throttle. Lean forward and down. Move to the side of the road as soon as possible.

questions.question: When parking a motorcycle next to a curb, position it:

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with both wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the space so drivers can see it easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: Riding next to another vehicle:

options.text: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
Is better than riding behind the vehicle.
Is safe because it limits your escape routes.
Should only be done during daytime.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to other vehicles. The driver may not see you in their blind spot and could move into your lane. Riding alongside also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Hold onto the seat.
Place their feet on the muffler.
Get on after you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Start your engine before your passenger gets on. They should sit as far forward as comfortable and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt. They must keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best formation is:

options.text: In pairs.
In a staggered line.
In a single-file line.
In a passing formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered line.
questions.explanation: A staggered line keeps the group close while giving each rider enough space to stay safe. Ride single-file in curves, turns, or when entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: Which provides the best face protection?

options.text: Sunglasses
Windshield
Goggles
Face shield

questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
Taking artificial stimulants.
Limiting your riding distance each day.
Taking frequent breaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: Take breaks often and avoid riding more than six hours per day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain—they cause fatigue. Never use artificial stimulants. When they wear off, you become very tired and unsafe.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid it.
Change lanes quickly.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare it away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Avoid hitting animals when you safely can. In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving could cause you to crash into another vehicle, which is worse than hitting a small animal.

questions.question: A windshield:

options.text: Works as well as a face shield.
Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
Is required on all motorcycles.
Should be used only on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.
